b.answer:
Worked example: Crestline Uniforms, a fictional school-uniform maker in Abeokuta selling to private schools.

Objects: contacts (bursars, proprietors), companies (schools), deals (a term's uniform order), activities.

StageExit rule (move on when…)Win chance
New enquiryA school has asked for prices or samples10%
Samples deliveredSamples are at the school and signed for25%
Quote sentA written price and delivery date has been sent50%
Deposit paidThe school has paid the deposit75%
Won / LostOrder delivered and paid, or the school said no (with a reason)100% / 0%

Custom properties (7 of 10): lead_source (dropdown), marketing_consent, consent_date, school_type (nursery/primary/secondary), pupils_estimate, term_value_ngn, lost_reason (dropdown).

Owners: Mrs Odu (schools over 300 pupils), Tayo (all others).

Four dashboard numbers: open deal value by stage; deals in the same stage over 14 days; won and lost this month with reasons; new deals by lead_source.

The owner agreed each stage is something the school does, not something we hope.
mistakes: Stages named after feelings ('Very interested', 'Will call back').
More than 10 custom properties, or free-text fields for source and lost reason.
Mixing lifecycle stages with deal stages in one list.
Owners named as 'sales' instead of people.
b.pass: A one-page design with objects, five or so stages each with an exit rule the customer meets and a win chance, up to 10 custom properties, named owners, the four dashboard numbers, and the owner's agreement.
b.redo: Send it back if any stage lacks an exit rule or describes a hope, properties exceed 10, or the owner has not agreed.

s.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane in HubSpot's free CRM. (Zoho: same steps under Setup → Customization.)

  1. Sign up with Harvest Lane's domain email. Settings → Objects → Deals → Pipelines: rename stages to New enquiry, Tasting booked, Proposal sent, Trial order, Won / Lost with 10, 25, 50, 75, 100/0%.
  2. 8 custom properties: lead_source, marketing_consent, consent_date (contact); business_type, delivery_zone (company); weekly_value_ngn, lost_reason, next_step_date (deal). That is 8, leaving 2 spare (one goes to harvest_score in 5.9).
  3. Clean the Growth Desk export with the Card 4 checklist, then import companies, then contacts (matched by domain), then deals. 10 rows first, check associations, then the rest.
  4. Every open deal gets Tolu or Bisi as owner and a next_step_date. Saved view: "My deals needing a next step".
ImportRowsDuplicates found in cleaning
Companies143 (www. and no-domain versions of Bodija Suites, one Grill Yard)
Contacts172 (same email in different case)
Deals90

40 records, all associated: every deal shows its company and contact.

Monday dashboard, first week

ReportValue
Open value by stage (weekly)New enquiry ₦410,000 · Tasting ₦300,000 · Proposal ₦520,000 · Trial ₦180,000
Stuck over 14 days2 (Mama Put Express, Kakanfo Inn)
Won / lost this month1 won · 1 lost (current supplier)
New deals by sourceInstagram 3 · outreach 2 · referral 1
mistakes: Importing everything at once without a 10-row test.
Importing contacts before companies, so contacts are not matched by domain.
Leaving 'www.' on some domains, creating duplicate companies.
Deals with no owner or next step date.
s.pass: Screenshots show at least 30 imported records with every deal associated to a company and contact, no duplicates, every open deal with an owner and next step, and a dashboard showing all four numbers.
s.redo: Send it back if duplicates remain, any deal is unassociated or ownerless, fewer than 30 records were imported, or a dashboard number is missing.

g.answer:
Worked example: Crestline Uniforms (fictional), four Monday reviews in HubSpot's free CRM with the owner and two staff.

ReviewOpen dealsStuck 14+ daysWhat happened to the stuck dealsUpdated by team?
Week 12373 got a call booked; 2 closed Lost (chose another supplier); 2 had no owner, now assignedPartly: owner did most
Week 2254Greenfield College moved to Deposit paid after a call; 1 Lost (budget)Yes, both staff
Week 32432 re-quoted with a new delivery dateYes
Week 4262Both have next steps this weekYes

Rescued: Greenfield College (₦1.4m term order) had sat at Quote sent for 19 days; the call showed they were waiting for a sample blazer. It was delivered, and they paid the deposit.

Honestly closed: 4 deals moved to Lost with reasons, so the open pipeline fell from ₦9.1m to ₦6.3m, a more believable forecast.

Training: one 40-minute session and the mobile app installed on both phones. Activity logged by staff rose from 6 to 31 entries a week.

Next: the owner keeps the 20-minute Monday review; 5.9 will automate the stuck-deal reminders.

Submit: the four dashboard screenshots, this table, the activity counts per person, and the rescued deal's timeline.
mistakes: Running reviews where only the learner updates the CRM.
Reporting stuck deals without saying what happened to them.
Keeping dead deals open to make the pipeline look bigger.
Skipping training and the mobile app.
g.pass: Four Monday reviews with stuck-deal counts and outcomes, evidence the team logged activity themselves each week, and at least one stuck deal rescued or honestly closed.
g.redo: Send it back if fewer than four reviews ran, the learner did all the updating, or no stuck deal was resolved.
